notes: Read all 35 source lines (numbered) before editing. The module is: the react import of useEffect/useState (L1), the import of getConnectionStatus/onStatusChange from '@/lib/resilience' (L2), the JSDoc header documenting the navigator.onLine + resilience-broadcaster backing, the PWA offline-banner / query-error / retry-when-online use cases, and the 'why not just navigator.onLine' rationale (L4-24), the exported useOnlineStatus(): boolean signature (L25), the useState seed `getConnectionStatus() === 'online'` (L26), the useEffect that subscribes via onStatusChange and maps `status === 'online'` to setOnline, returning the unsubscribe (L28-32), `return online` (L34), and the closing brace (L35). Every line was considered and ported.

Public contract preserved (rule 3): the exported `useOnlineStatus(): boolean` signature is byte-for-byte; the boolean derivation is unchanged (`status === 'online'`); the state variable is still named `online` with setter `setOnline`; the seed is still read lazily in the useState initializer; the subscription is still established in a `[]`-dep useEffect that returns a cleanup. No API paths, units, or i18n strings exist in this hook to preserve.

Conversion contract rule 7 (browser-only dependency -> native-safe impl): web L2 routes through `@/lib/resilience`, whose status broadcaster (resilience.ts L51/L60-61/L67) is built purely on the browser-only `navigator.onLine` read and the `window` `online`/`offline` events. None of those globals exist in the bare React Native runtime and the project ships no @react-native-community/netinfo dependency (verified in apps/native/package.json), so there is no OS connectivity stream to bind to. Following the same probe-then-degrade pattern proven in the useSSE parity port (which probes globalThis.EventSource), this hook feature-detects globalThis.navigator.onLine (readConnectionStatus) and the globalThis online/offline addEventListener/removeEventListener surface (getOnlineEventTarget). Under react-native-web and browsers these are present, so behavior matches the web hook exactly (seed from navigator.onLine; online event -> true, offline event -> false, mirroring resilience.ts setStatus mapping). On bare native they are absent, so the hook stays in an explicit, documented optimistic-online state: it returns true and attaches no listeners, so offline-only UI never false-positives on a platform that cannot observe connectivity, and request failures still surface through the api/client error path.

Deliberately does NOT route through the native api/client.ts getConnectionStatus(): that value is fetch-outcome derived, starts at 'unknown' (which would seed a spurious offline=false at first paint), and exposes no onStatusChange broadcaster, so it cannot honor the event-subscribed re-render contract the web hook guarantees. Rationale captured in the hook JSDoc and here for the next maintainer.

No DOM modules, browser HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, framer-motion, or old web UI components are imported (rules 4-5): the only import is `react` (useEffect, useState). Browser globals are reached exclusively through guarded `globalThis as typeof globalThis & {...}` casts (the same technique as useSSE.ts) because the React Native tsconfig (@react-native/typescript-config) omits the DOM lib, so navigator/addEventListener are not ambient. `as unknown as OnlineEventTarget` is used to bridge the `unknown`-typed probe, matching the existing useSSE pattern.

Style matched to the native tree (RN prettier: singleQuote, trailingComma all, arrowParens avoid, bracketSpacing false / no spaces inside braces; @react-native eslint; `== null`/`!= null` allowed as in useSSE.ts and api/client.ts) and the relative-import convention (no @/ alias; this hook needs no internal imports). Gates run green from apps/native: `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit, 0 errors), `npm run lint -- --quiet` (0 problems), `npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles` (all suites passed). In the jest react-native (node) env neither globalThis.addEventListener nor navigator.onLine is defined, so the hook deterministically seeds true and attaches no listeners — no open handles introduced.
